GENUINE Freescale application note AN1646, 'Noise Considerations for Integrated Pressure Sensors', Rev 2, 05/2005, 7 pp, FrameMaker 7.0, by Ador Reodique and Warren Schultz. Referenced by name from MPXV4006DP.pdf p.5 ('For additional output filtering, please refer to Application Note AN1646'). OUTPUT FILTERING, p.2 verbatim: 'a low-pass RC filter with a cutoff frequency of 650 Hz is recommended. A 750 ohm resistor and a 0.33 uF capacitor have been determined to give the best results (see Figure 2) since the 750 ohm series impedance is low enough for most A/D converters.' Figure 2 topology: sensor Vout -> 750 ohm series -> A/D node, 0.33 uF from that node to ground, supply decoupled 1.0 uF || 0.01 uF. calc: 1/(2*pi*750*0.33u) = 643 Hz, agrees with the stated 650. Figure 3 adds an MC33502 rail-to-rail buffer for A/Ds that cannot take the source impedance. Software: 8 to 64 sample rolling average; 10 samples -> ~2.5 mV pk-pk, 64 samples -> ~1 mV pk-pk, S/N improves as sqrt(N); four samples PLUS the RC filter also gives ~1 mV pk-pk. p.5 POWER SUPPLY: 5.0 V +/-5% supplying the sensor's maximum 10 mA; powering at any other voltage invalidates the offset, TCO and TCS trim; 0.33-1.0 uF || 0.01 uF ceramic decoupling; prefer a linear regulator such as MC78L05 over a switcher; tie the sensor supply and the A/D reference to the SAME supply so the output's ratiometricity cancels supply variation. p.5-6 LAYOUT: five rules (minimise loop areas; field-cancel by running equal opposite currents together; no 90-degree angles including T connections; single-point analog-to-power ground tie, made as close as possible to the A/D's VREFL; use ground planes selectively on analog boards), plus 'not advisable to have more than 1 inch between a de-coupling capacitor and the active device' with 50 mil traces. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: MOUNTING. There is NO mounting section and NO mounting-stress caution anywhere in the seven pages - that caution lives in Note 5 of MPXV4006DP.pdf p.3 ('external mechanical stresses and mounting position can affect the zero pressure output reading ... the device output must be autozeroed after installation ... assumes a maximum temperature change of +/-5 C between autozero and measurement'). NOTE ALSO that the datasheet's own Figure 3 output filter is a bare 470 pF with no series resistor, and the datasheet's accuracy curves are stated to be taken with THAT circuit, not with AN1646's 750 ohm / 0.33 uF - the two vendor recommendations are different circuits.

part: Sub-miniature toggle, 6.00 mm metric bushing - generic/Multicomp (the MTS-101 family)
notes: Multicomp 'Toggle Switches Sub-Miniature', 21/03/08 V1.1, 4 pages. THIS IS THE GENUINELY SUB-MINIATURE FAMILY - the one the BOM's 'MTS-101' guess was pointing at - and it is a DIFFERENT SIZE CLASS from the NKK Series M banked alongside it, which NKK calls MINIATURE. Dimensions read by rendering page 1 at 150 dpi; the drawings are vector. *** BUSHING IS A TRUE 6.00 mm DIAMETER WITH A FLAT AT 4.39 mm *** (marked '(phi 0.236) phi 6.00' and '(0.173) 4.39'), body front outline 8.13 x 5.08mm, bushing 5.59mm long, toggle 2.54mm dia x 9.40mm, 3 solder terminals on 2.54mm pitch, terminal field 1.52/0.60. Contact rating 0.4 VA maximum at 20V max AC or DC - SIGNAL LEVEL ONLY, which suits SW-POWER's job of driving an enable pin, and terminals are gold plated as standard. 30,000 cycles, -30 to +85C, 20 mohm max contact resistance. *** IT HAS NO SPST. *** Pole options are M2RE SPDT, M2RE DPDT, M6RE SPDT and M6RE DPDT only (M2RE/M6RE are TERMINAL styles, not bushing threads - do not misread them as an M6 thread code). So a true 6.00mm sub-miniature part exists but only as SPDT/DPDT, and an SPST has to be made by leaving one throw unconnected. BANKED AS THE SECOND HALF OF THE PANEL-HOLE ANSWER: this family needs a ~6.0-6.2mm hole with a 4.39mm flat, where the NKK M6x0.75 needs 6.5mm with a 5.6-5.8mm flat. MATED ARITHMETIC (calc, stated in the MECH report): H_mated = H_hdr + H_skt - D_cav; with the repo's Wurth header (9.10 above board, 6.50 cavity) and the 10.5 socket this is 13.10 mm, with the 3M header 13.30 mm, with TE's own header 13.86 mm; using the 12.10 MAX socket, 14.70 / 14.90 mm. 13.10 mm is a HARD LOWER BOUND because insertion depth cannot exceed cavity depth. WITH the strain-relief clip it becomes 16.95 mm nominal / 19.40 mm max, i.e. 3.1 mm or 0.6 mm of headroom - do not fit one. WHAT THIS DOCUMENT DOES NOT GIVE: any mated assembly drawing, any stated insertion depth, any cable-exit or bend height, and no cavity-depth dimension on the TE header (the 6.50 mm used above comes from the Wurth and 3M sheets already banked). The seating assumption - that the socket bottoms on the cavity floor - is an assumption, not a datasheet statement.

Pin/channel map, read from the p.1 Pinout vector diagram rendered at 200 dpi (it does not extract as text): PIN 2 IS THE COMMON/GROUND, and pins 1, 3, 4, 5 are the four protected channels, each a back-to-back avalanche+forward pair to the common rail. All four channels share ONE common pin - there is no per-channel ground, so a single array cannot straddle PWR_GND and DIG_GND, which supports keeping U-TVS-SPI and U-TVS-CHAIN as two separate packages. TWO FACTS THE BOM ROW'S PHRASE '4-channel 5V array' DOES NOT CONVEY: (1) the array is effectively UNI-DIRECTIONAL - the negative clamp of -0.4/-0.8/-1.2 V at -10 mA is a plain forward diode drop, not an avalanche knee (p.3 V-I curve confirms), so it protects a 0 to +5 V signal referenced to the common pin and must NOT be reused on a bipolar CV node; (2) 30 pF per channel is HIGH for a signal-line TVS (p.1 Applications lists USB1.1 - this is a low-speed part by design). For Woody's SPI2 at 2 MHz behind the 100 ohm R-SPI-SER the 30 pF is acceptable: it is about 23 percent of the line's total capacitance including ~100 pF of 2 m Cat5, giving roughly a 29 ns edge against a 250 ns half-period, but this is the first time TVS capacitance has entered the umbilical edge budget at all. onsemi MC74HC165A / MC74HCT165A '8-Bit Serial or Parallel-Input/Serial-Output Shift Register', publication MC74HC165A/D, Rev. 13, April 2025, 16 pp. THIS IS THE DOCUMENT THAT SETTLES THE 3.3 V THRESHOLD QUESTION, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE REPO. It is the only 74HC165 datasheet of the four banked that CHARACTERISES THE PART AT 3 V: DC ELECTRICAL CHARACTERISTICS p.4 has VCC columns 2.0 / 3.0 / 4.5 / 6.0 V, and the 3.0 V row reads VIH min = 2.1 V and VIL max = 0.9 V - EXACTLY 0.70 / 0.30 x VCC, the ratio config/figures.yaml currently asserts 'BREAKS' below 4.5 V. Values are absolute volts, test condition 'Vout = 0.1 V or VCC - 0.1 V, |Iout| <= 20 uA', guaranteed over -55 to 25C / <=85C / <=125C. 3 V is a fully characterised rail here, not a stray line: Recommended Operating Ranges p.3 carries tr,tf 0-600 ns at VCC = 3.0 V and the AC table p.4 carries 3.0 V rows throughout. CONSEQUENCE: 3.3 V is BRACKETED by two published 0.70/0.30 rows (3.0 V and 4.5 V), so interpolating needs no assumption - VIH(3.3) = 2.1 + 0.2 x (3.15-2.1) = 2.31 V and VIL(3.3) = 0.9 + 0.2 x (1.35-0.9) = 0.99 V, which restore key-release-time to 119.9 us and key-press-time to 5.92 us. Transferability rests on all four banked 74HC165 documents agreeing digit for digit at every shared rail (2.0 V 1.5/0.5; 4.5 V 3.15/1.35; 6.0 V 4.2/1.8), these being JEDEC HC family thresholds; bom.csv U-KEYS lists manufacturer 'multiple' so this part is itself a legitimate fit. CAVEAT: this is the 'A' speed grade and a different vendor from the banked TI SN74HC165, so its AC numbers are NOT interchangeable with TI's. Also covers, at the 3.0 V rail specifically: fmax 18 MHz, tPLH/tPHL clock to QH 52 ns max, SH/LD to QH 58 ns, input H to QH 52 ns, output transition 27 ns; plus Cin 10 pF max, ICC 4 uA max at 25C/6.0 V, CPD 40 pF typ, IIK/IOK +/-20 mA. Figure 1 p.1 pin assignments CONFIRM the repo's [from memory] pin map and that QHbar pin 7 is an output.

SETTLES THE 5V-vs-3V3 QUESTION: all 64 LEDs have pin 1 VDD on net VCC_5V and pin 3 VSS on GND - no regulator, load switch, P-FET or diode between VCC_5V and the array. VCC_5V is USB VBUS through ONE SCHOTTKY, D1 = B5819WS (anode pin 1 on VBUS, cathode pin 2 = VCC_5V), so the LED rail is VBUS minus one Vf, NOT 5.00 V; C1 2.2uF sits on the VBUS side of D1. THE LED PART IS WS2812B-0807, NOT WS2812C - 64 instances U1..U64, value string verified on every symbol; this REFUTES ADR 0007 line 176, ROADMAP line 184 and ADR 0014 line 358, and the 5 mA/channel and 960 mA figures that rest on the WS2812C-2020 datasheet. DATA LINE: IO14 -> Q1 DMG1012T-7 N-channel MOSFET level shifter (gate pin 1 to 3V3, source pin 2 = IO14 with R4 2.2K pull-up to 3V3, drain pin 3 = LED_DIN with R3 4.7K pull-up to VCC_5V); NO SERIES RESISTOR anywhere on the data line; LED_DIN enters U8 pin 4 and the chain runs U8->U7->U6...->DOUT. 3V3 RAIL: U49 = ME6217C33M5G, pin 1 VIN from VCC_5V, pin 3 EN tied to VIN, pin 4 BP not connected, pin 5 VOUT = 3V3; input C3 0.1uF + C4 10uF, output C2 10uF. The 800 mA rating the manifest carries for this LDO is NOT on the schematic and remains unsourced. DECOUPLING ON THE LED RAIL: NONE INSIDE THE ARRAY - C1..C18 bounding boxes were extracted and none falls within the array extent; total VCC_5V capacitance is 11.1uF (C5 1uF at Q1, C3 0.1uF + C4 10uF at the LDO input). Extension pads are TP1 = DOUT, TP2 = VCC_5V, TP3 = GND. Also carries: MCU U66 = ESP32-S3FH4R2, R7/R9 22R in series on USB_N/USB_P, Y1 40MHz, J2 chip antenna CA-C03, IMU U67 = QMI8658C, R1/R2 5.1K CC pulldowns, header P1 20 pins.
